title: SettingsClient.setApiKey / ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.setApiKey
description: Messages of the SettingsClient.setApiKey() method (agent-settings-contract task 1.5). This is the single secret write path of the client contract: set() carries no key field, so every key replace goes through here and every clear through clearApiKey. On the Desktop bridge (IPC channel ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.setApiKey) the main process stores the key write-only into safeStorage (the Keychain) and applies it to the sidecar (desktop-agent-settings-bridge 1.2); the renderer never sees it again. On HTTP it maps to PUT on the settings route with backend.api_key, refused with secrets_not_accepted when agent.settings.accept_secrets is false (on LKE the key is set out-of-band as a Kubernetes Secret, ADR-0009 section 5, and the UI replaces the field with 'Set on the server (Kubernetes Secret)', webui-agent-settings-page 1.2). Key material never appears in any response, log or event.

revision.description: The current revision as returned by get() or a previous mutation. Maps to the HTTP If-Match header; a stale value is rejected with revision_conflict (412).

api_key.description: The new key. Write-only: it is never returned by get(), status() or any event, and never echoed in an error.

kind.description: Which backend kind the key is for. Absent means the kind of the backend currently selected in the caller (first run) or configured (thereafter). Lets the first-run form stage a key before the backend itself is applied with set().

revision.description: The new revision after the apply.

SetApiKeyResponse.description: Reports key presence and provenance only. The stored key itself is never returned.

set.description: Whether a key is configured. True after a successful setApiKey.

source.description: Where the configured key comes from (settings_api after this call). Present exactly when set is true.

ApiKeyStatus.description: Mirrors ../settings-read.schema.json ApiKeyStatus. There is no field that can carry key material.
